slides.title: Streaming Media Over Networks
slides.body:
Streaming Stored Audio/Video
Streaming allows playback while the media is being received, without waiting for the full file to download.

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Why is it useful?
Instant access No waiting for full download
Smooth playback with proper Pre-loading
Saves local storage

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body: Types of Streaming

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Types of Streaming
Must download the entire file first
Example: Downloading a movie to watch later
Download-and-Play

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Types of Streaming
Streaming
Playback starts immediately as data arrives
No need to download the full file
Example: YouTube on-demand video

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Types of Streaming
Progressive Download
The file starts downloading, and playback begins once enough data is buffered but the file is downloaded linearly (start to end)

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Types of Streaming
Podcast apps downloading episodes, older HTML5 video players, downloading a song on a music app while listening
Netflix and YouTube do NOT use progressive download,  they use Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (HLS/DASH), which is more advanced

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Streaming Problems
Delay (Latency)
Delay before content starts playing
Buffering
Video pauses to load more data
Packet Loss
 Missing data causes glitches

slides.title: Streaming Stored Audio/Video
slides.body:
Streaming Problems
Jitter
Uneven arrival of packets →  video/audio plays unevenly
Bandwidth Variation
Network speed changes affect quality

slides.body:
How Media Reaches User?
Message Type
Direction
RTSP

Purpose
Controls media playback (play, pause, seek) like a TV remote for streaming
Example
CCTV cameras, IP cameras, older media players

slides.title: Streaming Protocols
slides.body:
How Media Reaches User?
Message Type
Direction
HLS
HTTP Live Streaming
Purpose
Breaks video into small chunks (.ts files) and delivers over HTTP. Adapts quality based on your internet speed
Example
YouTube, Netflix, Apple devices, Instagram

slides.title: Streaming Protocols
slides.body:
How Media Reaches User?
Message Type
Direction
DASH

Purpose
Similar to HLS  adapts video quality in real-time based on network conditions. Open standard (not Apple-only)
Example
YouTube, Netflix, Amazon Prime

slides.title: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR)
slides.body:
Behind Buffer-Free Viewing
Server stores video in MULTIPLE quality levels
240p, 360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p
Player checks your current internet speed

slides.title: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR)
slides.body:
Behind Buffer-Free Viewing
Player automatically picks the best quality → Fast internet? 1080p HD → Slow internet? → 480p SD → Speed drops mid-video? → Switches down seamlessly
Video plays without buffering!

slides.title: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR)
slides.body:
Behind Buffer-Free Viewing
Both HLS and DASH use this technique. This is why Netflix and YouTube rarely buffer they ADAPT to your network instead of trying to force HD on a slow connection

slides.title: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR)
slides.body:
Analogy
ABR is like a smart water tap when water pressure is high, it gives full flow (HD), When pressure drops, it reduces flow (lower quality) but never stops completely, You always get water (video) without interruption

slides.title: Real-Time Media Protocols
slides.body: Real-Time Media Protocols

slides.title: Real-Time Transport Protocol
slides.body:
RTP (Real-Time Transport Protocol)
Why it’s used
Ensures smooth delivery of media packets
Helps maintain timing of audio/video
What is RTP
A protocol used to send real-time audio and video over the Internet

slides.title: Real-Time Transport Protocol
slides.body:
What RTP does?
Adds timestamps → Tells the receiver WHEN each packet should be played (keeps audio/video timed correctly)
Payload Type Identification → Tells receiver what media type is inside (codec info)
Adds sequence numbers → Tells the receiver the ORDER of packets (detects missing or out-of-order packets)

slides.title: Real-Time Transport Protocol
slides.body:
What RTP does?
RTP does NOT fix jitter by itself. It provides the metadata (timestamps + sequence numbers) that the receiver's jitter buffer uses to reorder and smooth out playback

slides.title: Real-Time Transport Protocol
slides.body:
Analogy
Think of RTP like a postal service that stamps every letter with a number and date, If letters arrive out of order, YOU (the receiver/jitter buffer) can rearrange them using the numbers, The postal service (RTP) didn't rearrange them it just gave you the information to do it yourself

Introduction
What is RTCP?
RTCP works with RTP to provide feedback on media delivery. It does not carry media itself

slides.title: Real-Time Transport Control Protocol
slides.body:
What RTCP Provides?
QoS Reports → How well the stream is performing
Packet Loss Reports → Identifies network issues
Delay Measurements → Helps detect latency
Audio/Video Sync → Keeps voice and video aligned

slides.title: Real-Time Transport Control Protocol
slides.body:
Purpose
RTCP Purpose
Improves streaming quality by reporting problems so systems can adjust

slides.title: Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP)
slides.body:
What is VoIP?
VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol)
VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is a technology that allows voice calls to be transmitted over the Internet instead of traditional telephone lines
WhatsApp voice call
Skype
Zoom audio call

slides.body:
Analogy
Think of the SIP server as a receptionist at a hotel  when you call someone, the receptionist (SIP server) finds out which room (IP address) the person is in and connects your call

slides.body:
Analogy
The VoIP Gateway is like a translator if one person speaks digital (VoIP) and the other speaks analog (landline), the gateway translates between the two

slides.title: VoIP Protocols
slides.body:
SIP (Session Initiation Protocol)
The MOST widely used VoIP signaling protocol today
Handles: Setting up, modifying, and tearing down voice/video calls
Works like HTTP text-based, uses requests and responses

slides.title: VoIP Protocols
slides.body:
SIP (Session Initiation Protocol)
SIP Messages
INVITE
Start a call
ACK
Confirm call setup
BYE
End the call
REGISTER
Register your device with SIP server
Used by: WhatsApp, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, most modern VoIP systems

slides.title: VoIP Protocols
slides.body:
H.323 (ITU-T Standard)
An older, more complex VoIP protocol suite
Was the dominant VoIP standard before SIP

slides.title: VoIP Protocols
slides.body:
H.323 (ITU-T Standard)
Multiple Sub Protocols
H.225
Call signaling
H.245
Media control
RTP
Media transport
Still used in: Legacy enterprise video conferencing, older telecom systems
More complex than SIP but very feature-rich

slides.title: VoIP Protocols
slides.body:
Analogy
SIP vs H.323 is like WhatsApp vs a Fax Machine, Both can send messages, but WhatsApp (SIP) is simpler, faster, and what everyone uses today, Fax machines (H.323) still exist in some offices but they're the older, more complex way of doing things
